{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My attention to detail made me the best editor in the department. Then I started catching errors everywhere—in menus, street signs, texts from friends. I couldn't read anything without correcting it. My wife left because I wouldn't stop editing her emails. The skill that built my career destroyed my marriage.

CANDIDATE A:
My attention to detail made me a good editor, but I learned early to compartmentalize. At work, I'm meticulous. At home, I let the small stuff go. My wife jokes that I have an 'off switch.' The balance keeps both my career and marriage healthy.

CANDIDATE B:
My empathy made me an exceptional therapist. I could feel what my clients felt. Then I couldn't turn it off. I absorbed everyone's pain—strangers on the subway, characters in movies. I had a breakdown and couldn't practice for two years. My greatest gift became my heaviest burden.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:16"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both the situation and Candidate B describe a skill that initially led to professional success but eventually became overwhelming and detrimental to personal well-being."}
